request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: fire-damaged pitched roof with exposed charred rafters
red brick Victorian villa with chimneys
street frontage with pavement, boundary wall and road

damaged_parts.condition: burnt through, charred timbers exposed, roof covering largely missing
window opening blackened, sash appears burnt or missing
tiles missing or collapsed over the left part of the roof

materials: cast iron or metal guttering and downpipes
visible_items: brick chimney stacks with clay pots
regional_indicators: UK-format number plate with yellow rear plate
vehicle driving on the left side of the road
parsed_output.summary_en: A red brick Victorian-style house on a street corner shows severe fire damage to its roof, with charred exposed rafters, missing roof covering and a blackened upper side window. Barrier tape and traffic cones sit near the front boundary wall, and the lower brickwork and ground floor windows appear largely intact.
